edges.process: Form-dependent folate processing and folate-cycle conversion supply 5-methyltetrahydrofolate; folic acid requires reduction.
edges.limitations: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

evidence.statement: Dietary folate, including folic acid reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, is converted through the folate cycle to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor used by methionine synthase.

edges.process: Absorbed cobalamin undergoes intracellular processing to methylcobalamin used by methionine synthase.
edges.limitations: Provision of vitamin B12 does not show that increasing intake raises tissue remethylation flux. Added vitamin B12 further lowered blood homocysteine beyond folic acid in pooled trials, which remains a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

evidence.statement: Dietary cobalamin is absorbed and processed intracellularly to the methylcobalamin cofactor used by methionine synthase.

edges.process: Choline oxidation supplies betaine upstream of BHMT.
edges.limitations: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved. Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. The enzyme evidence uses purified or recombinant human protein, not intact human metabolism. Loss of activity after removing zinc ligands does not show that dietary zinc usually limits the enzyme. The review statement that the pathway is independent of folate and vitamin B12 is not a new flux experiment. Quantitative claims in that review about choline deficiency and liver methionine were not re-checked in the primary animal papers. Purified, stable human choline dehydrogenase has been difficult to obtain, so some catalytic detail is inferred from related enzymes and from tissue activity rather than from a complete human kinetic characterisation. The reviews do not show that raising choline intake increases BHMT flux in people.

evidence.statement: Dietary precursor that can be oxidised to betaine, the methyl-donor substrate for BHMT

edges.process: Protein digestion and amino-acid absorption provide methionine to the methionine cycle.
edges.limitations: Dietary protein supplies methionine. It does not show that eating more protein increases cycle rates. DIAAS scores sulfur amino acids as methionine plus cysteine. The pathway accounts are reviews. Transsulfuration is not present in every tissue. The human rate study was a 28-day vitamin B6 restriction in nine healthy young adults. It does not show that ordinary changes in methionine, folate, or B-vitamin intake change those rates. Individual enzyme reactions remain neighbouring mechanisms.

evidence.statement: Provides digestible methionine, the amino acid that enters the cycle.

edges.process: Methionine can supply cysteine through upstream transsulfuration before glutathione assembly.
edges.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis. All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

evidence.statement: Dietary methionine can supply cysteine for glutathione assembly. Methionine is not a substrate of the assembly enzymes.

edges.process: Supplemental N-acetylcysteine supplies a cysteine precursor in the tested combined glycine protocol.
edges.limitations: The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result. All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

evidence.statement: Supplemental cysteine precursor given with glycine to older adults, in whom erythrocyte glutathione synthesis increased.

edges.process: Riboflavin supplies the precursor for FMN used by complex I.
edges.limitations: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context. The sources are reviews of enzyme structure and function, not human feeding trials. Flavin mononucleotide (FMN) abundance has not been shown to limit complex I in ordinary conditions. Endogenous ubiquinone synthesis is not separated here from dietary coenzyme Q10. Copper and iron centres are not evidence that supplements raise chain activity.

evidence.statement: Riboflavin is the vitamin precursor of flavin mononucleotide (FMN), the flavin that accepts NADH electrons in complex I.

edges.process: Tyrosine-derived headgroup carbon enters CoQ10 through 4-HPP, HPDL-associated 4-HMA and 4-HB formation followed by prenylation and COQ maturation; this is a net precursor relationship, not an assertion that all intervening human enzymes are assigned.
edges.limitations: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established. Endogenous phenylalanine conversion is an alternative source; the full human intervening enzyme sequence remains incompletely assigned.

evidence.statement: Human-cell isotope tracing and genetic rescue support net tyrosine contribution; no dietary conversion yield is assumed.

edges.process: Multistep hepatic kynurenine/de-novo NAD metabolism and subsequent nicotinamide availability for salvage; not a direct one-step tryptophan-to-nicotinamide reaction.
edges.limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺. This is a review of pathways, not a human feeding trial. It does not measure how much an ordinary meal changes NAD⁺, and it does not test attention or cognitive energy. Nicotinamide riboside and nicotinamide mononucleotide, as supplement doses, are outside this dietary assessment.

evidence.statement: The liver can convert tryptophan to nicotinamide, which other cells salvage into NAD⁺.

edges.process: Human NRK1 phosphorylates beta-NR to beta-NMN using ATP.
edges.limitations: An established intracellular route is not proof that all oral NR reaches each tissue intact; parallel degradation/salvage can contribute.

evidence.statement: NRK1 curated reaction, entry version 170, Rhea 14017, retrieved 26 October 2026.

edges.process: NMN adenylyltransferase adenylates oxidised beta-NMN with ATP to form oxidised NAD.
edges.limitations: NMNAT1 establishes reaction identity; other isoforms/transport determine compartmental provision. No fixed dietary conversion yield or mitochondrial/brain endpoint is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human NMNAT1, entry version 202, Rhea 21360, retrieved 26 October 2026.

edges.process: Digestive lipolysis releases C8 fatty acid from trioctanoin; the absorbed fatty acid is represented as octanoate at physiological pH.
edges.limitations: The C8 acyl form is not free octanoate content in food. Mixed-chain MCT products have formulation-dependent composition.

edges.process: Hepatic fatty-acid activation and successive mitochondrial beta-oxidation reactions generate acetyl-CoA from the C8 chain.
edges.limitations: This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions.

evidence.statement: Human medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase establishes the initial beta-oxidation reaction; the clinical exposure additionally measures downstream ketone provision.

edges.process: Hepatic mitochondrial ketogenesis proceeds through acetoacetyl-CoA formation, HMG-CoA synthase and HMG-CoA lyase to produce acetoacetate.
dependencies: Ketone release, circulation and brain monocarboxylate transport
edges.limitations: The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

evidence.statement: Curated human ACAT1, HMGCS2 and HMGCL reactions, retrieved 26 October 2026.

edges.process: Hydrolysis of ellagitannins releases ellagic acid in the gut lumen.

edges.process: Gut microbial conversion of ellagic acid through intermediate urolithins to urolithin A.

edges.limitations: Non-producers form little or no urolithin A; the species studied did not complete conversion alone.

conversion_pathway.process: Form-dependent folate processing and folate-cycle conversion supply 5-methyltetrahydrofolate; folic acid requires reduction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

evidence.statement: Dietary folate, including folic acid reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, is converted through the folate cycle to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor used by methionine synthase.

conversion_pathway.process: Choline oxidation supplies betaine upstream of BHMT.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved. Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. The enzyme evidence uses purified or recombinant human protein, not intact human metabolism. Loss of activity after removing zinc ligands does not show that dietary zinc usually limits the enzyme. The review statement that the pathway is independent of folate and vitamin B12 is not a new flux experiment. Quantitative claims in that review about choline deficiency and liver methionine were not re-checked in the primary animal papers. Purified, stable human choline dehydrogenase has been difficult to obtain, so some catalytic detail is inferred from related enzymes and from tissue activity rather than from a complete human kinetic characterisation. The reviews do not show that raising choline intake increases BHMT flux in people.

evidence.statement: Dietary precursor that can be oxidised to betaine, the methyl-donor substrate for BHMT

conversion_pathway.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

evidence.statement: Dietary methionine can supply cysteine for glutathione assembly. Methionine is not a substrate of the assembly enzymes.

paths.mission: Sustain efficient electron transport so mitochondria generate ATP without excessive electron leakage.

conversion_pathway.process: Riboflavin supplies the precursor for FMN used by complex I.
conversion_pathway.limitations: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context. The sources are reviews of enzyme structure and function, not human feeding trials. Flavin mononucleotide (FMN) abundance has not been shown to limit complex I in ordinary conditions. Endogenous ubiquinone synthesis is not separated here from dietary coenzyme Q10. Copper and iron centres are not evidence that supplements raise chain activity.

evidence.statement: Riboflavin is the vitamin precursor of flavin mononucleotide (FMN), the flavin that accepts NADH electrons in complex I.

paths.mission: Maintain endogenous Coenzyme Q synthesis, maturation and pool availability to support mitochondrial electron transfer and cellular redox functions.

conversion_pathway.process: Tyrosine-derived headgroup carbon enters CoQ10 through 4-HPP, HPDL-associated 4-HMA and 4-HB formation followed by prenylation and COQ maturation; this is a net precursor relationship, not an assertion that all intervening human enzymes are assigned.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established. evidence.statement: Human-cell isotope tracing and genetic rescue support net tyrosine contribution; no dietary conversion yield is assumed.

paths.mission: Maintain NAD⁺ availability so redox reactions and mitochondrial signalling stay adequately powered.

conversion_pathway.process: Multistep hepatic kynurenine/de-novo NAD metabolism and subsequent nicotinamide availability for salvage; not a direct one-step tryptophan-to-nicotinamide reaction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺. This is a review of pathways, not a human feeding trial. It does not measure how much an ordinary meal changes NAD⁺, and it does not test attention or cognitive energy. Nicotinamide riboside and nicotinamide mononucleotide, as supplement doses, are outside this dietary assessment.

evidence.statement: The liver can convert tryptophan to nicotinamide, which other cells salvage into NAD⁺.

paths.limitations: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

paths.mission: Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.

conversion_pathway.process: Human AGAT transfers the amidino group of arginine to glycine, yielding guanidinoacetate and ornithine.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Both co-substrates are required; this is not a fixed dietary yield or an assertion that extra intake is rate-limiting.

evidence.statement: UniProt P50440 entry version 227, Rhea 13201; human renal GAA production independently measured.

conversion_pathway.process: GAMT methylates guanidinoacetate using S-adenosylmethionine to form creatine.
dependencies: Interorgan exchange and receiving-tissue creatine transport
conversion_pathway.limitations: Reaction identity does not prove dietary precursor limitation or cerebral delivery; SAM participation creates no independent methionine admission.

evidence.statement: UniProt Q14353 entry version 215, Rhea 10656.

paths.limitations: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

paths.mission: Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.

conversion_pathway.process: Human AGAT transfers the amidino group of arginine to glycine, yielding guanidinoacetate and ornithine.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Both co-substrates are required; this is not a fixed dietary yield or an assertion that extra intake is rate-limiting.

evidence.statement: UniProt P50440 entry version 227, Rhea 13201; human renal GAA production independently measured.

conversion_pathway.process: GAMT methylates guanidinoacetate using S-adenosylmethionine to form creatine.
dependencies: Interorgan exchange and receiving-tissue creatine transport
conversion_pathway.limitations: Reaction identity does not prove dietary precursor limitation or cerebral delivery; SAM participation creates no independent methionine admission.

paths.limitations: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

paths.mission: Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.

conversion_pathway.process: MAT1A/MAT2A catalyse ATP-dependent methionine adenosylation to form SAM.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Reaction identity establishes capacity, not a universal limiting intake or greater flux from additional intake.

evidence.statement: Human MAT crystallography and curated Rhea 21080; P31153 v237 and Q00266 v233.

inventory.title: Light–Dark Circadian Entrainment

inventory.title: Feeding-Time Circadian Synchronisation

inventory.title: Melatonin Biosynthesis & Availability
inventory.mission: Support the body's capacity to synthesise melatonin from serotonin through the availability of essential precursors and the activity of its biosynthetic enzymes.

canonical_inputs.role: Tryptophan is the dietary precursor of serotonin, and serotonin is the substrate for melatonin formation. Severe depletion lowered nocturnal melatonin secretion.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Depletion shows a constraint. It does not show that extra dietary tryptophan raises melatonin. BRS1 admission is not inherited.

canonical_inputs.role: SAM is the methyl donor for ASMT. Dietary provision is indirect, through the methylation pathways that already own SAM synthesis.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Not a direct dietary requirement. Folate, vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and iron are not admitted on this PM.

canonical_inputs.role: Acetyl-CoA is the acetyl donor for AANAT. It is not a dietary acetyl-CoA requirement.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Pantothenate remains on BRS1 acetylcholine synthesis. It is not admitted here.

traceability_gaps.limitation: Depletion shows a constraint. It does not show that extra dietary tryptophan raises melatonin. BRS1 admission is not inherited.

inventory.title: NAPE → NAE Biosynthesis Capacity
inventory.mission: Enable NAPE-to-NAE biosynthesis so endocannabinoidome signalling lipids remain available for stress and motivation regulation.

canonical_inputs.role: NAPE supplies the acyl-ethanolamine moiety released during NAE formation.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Intracellular phospholipid provision does not establish a requirement to consume NAPE or phosphatidylethanolamine.

canonical_inputs.role: Intracellular phosphatidylethanolamine supplies the backbone used to form N-acyl phosphatidylethanolamine.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Intracellular phospholipid provision does not establish a requirement to consume NAPE or phosphatidylethanolamine.

canonical_inputs.role: Two active-site zinc ions support human NAPE-PLD hydrolysis.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Human enzyme structure and catalysis establish the metal dependency, not dietary zinc-driven brain NAE flux or benefit above adequacy. Cellular zinc homeostasis and membrane substrate access constrain loading; no extra-zinc recommendation is established.

inventory.title: Omega-3-Derived Endocannabinoidome Signalling
inventory.mission: Sustain omega-3-derived ethanolamide production so endocannabinoidome neuromodulation stays supplied from dietary fat status.

canonical_inputs.role: DHA supplies the acyl chain used to form N-docosahexaenoyl-PE and synaptamide.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Labelled neural-cell precursor experiments support formation; controlled oral-oil studies support corresponding plasma ethanolamide availability. Plasma concentration is not neuronal synthesis flux or receptor engagement, and no ordinary-food effective dose or clinical benefit is established. Direct is relative to this biosynthetic operation, not direct food content of synaptamide.

canonical_inputs.role: EPA supply supports formation of its corresponding ethanolamide, EPEA.
canonical_inputs.limitation: The oral EPA/DHA intervention evidence measures circulating corresponding ethanolamides, not neuronal synthesis rates or independent clinical mediation. Preserve active-arm, formulation and mixture limits. Direct refers to substrate provision to production; food EPA content is not food EPEA content or a quantified conversion yield.

inventory.title: FAAH-Mediated Endocannabinoid Preservation
inventory.mission: Preserve endocannabinoid signalling duration by limiting FAAH-mediated degradation of anandamide and related NAEs.

canonical_inputs.role: Anandamide is a signalling lipid hydrolysed by FAAH; inhibition can prolong its effects.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Administered anandamide and experimental inhibitors do not establish food efficacy or everyday motivational improvement.

canonical_inputs.role: Genistein is a soy isoflavone. Laboratory assays found that it altered anandamide uptake. That makes it a hypothesis candidate for dietary modulation of FAAH-mediated signal duration, not an admitted food lever.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Food-level genistein exposure to relevant neural FAAH inhibition and signal duration is unestablished. Dietary soy is not equivalent to unbound aglycone concentrations at neuronal FAAH. Soy, tofu, tempeh and edamame document occurrence only.

inventory.title: Endocannabinoid–Dopamine Neuromodulation

canonical_inputs.role: Endogenous 2-AG signalling contributes to VTA CB1-dependent reward-cue dopamine modulation.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Local pharmacology is not a dietary intervention or a general motivation benefit.

inventory.title: Endocannabinoid Stress-Buffering Capacity
inventory.mission: Sustain endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering so HPA-axis and neuroinflammatory reactivity stay proportionate.

inventory.mission: Maintain stable oestrogen-linked signalling so dopamine tone and emotional regulation remain steady across hormonal fluctuation.

canonical_inputs.role: Specific microbial beta-glucuronidases release free estrogens from conjugated substrates.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Not every glucuronidase performs the same reaction; whole-body estrogen recycling and food control were not established.

canonical_inputs.role: This host-derived steroid supplies the substrate for the studied microbial progestin conversion.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Microbial progestin formation is not demonstrated progesterone stability, systemic exposure, or a fibre intervention.

canonical_inputs.limitation: Microbial progestin formation is not demonstrated progesterone stability, systemic exposure, or a fibre intervention.

inventory.title: Metabolic-Reproductive Hormone Integration

inventory.title: Testosterone Signalling Stability
inventory.mission: Maintain androgen receptor signalling so motivation, stamina, and goal-directed effort remain well supported.

canonical_inputs.role: Adequate zinc supply supports testosterone availability; restriction and repletion studies identify a conditional upstream contribution to androgen ligand supply.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Small non-placebo comparisons; no androgen-receptor activity, motivation endpoint or benefit in zinc-replete people.

canonical_inputs.role: Dietary zinc maintains the metal pool supporting the androgen receptor’s zinc-finger DNA-binding capacity.
canonical_inputs.limitation: This Type A relationship concerns the receptor DNA-binding domain, not stimulation of testosterone production, tissue receptor occupancy, motivation or benefit from extra zinc. Cellular zinc homeostasis and receptor expression constrain metal availability. The primary crystal used an engineered rat receptor domain; human domain identity is curated. A zinc-finger mutation study tested an arginine substitution, not dietary zinc depletion.

traceability_gaps.limitation: Small non-placebo comparisons; no androgen-receptor activity, motivation endpoint or benefit in zinc-replete people.

canonical_inputs.role: Microbial metabolism releases free androgens from conjugated substrates within intestinal contents.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Luminal androgen metabolism does not establish circulating androgen supply or receptor effects in the brain.

inventory.title: Circulating Sex-Hormone Availability & Regulation
inventory.mission: Regulate measured circulating sex-hormone availability. Production, transport, metabolism and clearance are separate parts of that availability. A measurement of one part does not establish the others. The operation stops before receptor binding and downstream signalling. It does not judge a higher or lower concentration as benefit or harm.

inventory.title: Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation
inventory.mission: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

canonical_inputs.role: Coverage of the indispensable amino-acid set, including phenylalanine, that sets the circulating pool neurotransmitter pathways can draw on. Meals contribute measurable amino-acid composition; this is not a requirement that each meal provide complete coverage
canonical_inputs.limitation: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

canonical_inputs.role: Catecholamine precursor in the circulating pool this PM prioritises. Tyrosine is normally formed from indispensable phenylalanine and can become conditionally indispensable when phenylalanine availability is limited
canonical_inputs.limitation: Dietary supply to a circulating pool is distinct from brain transport, catecholamine synthesis or clinical benefit. A small human study found higher plasma tyrosine during protein-containing meals and after a large tyrosine supplement; it does not define ordinary-food efficacy or a need for extra tyrosine when supply is adequate. Tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

canonical_inputs.role: Indispensable serotonergic precursor this PM prioritises in the circulating precursor pool
canonical_inputs.limitation: Pool presence of tryptophan is not evidence for increased brain serotonin, brain entry, or an attention or mood benefit.

canonical_inputs.limitation: Competitive transport biology does not establish that eating more tyrosine increases brain tyrosine or catecholamine signalling.

canonical_inputs.role: Large-neutral amino acid that competes for LAT1-mediated brain entry
canonical_inputs.limitation: Meal-driven changes in plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratios do not establish increased brain serotonin or a clinical benefit.

canonical_inputs.limitation: Human intake-to-dopamine responsiveness and clinical benefit were not established; the direct dopamine-metabolite evidence assessed here is preclinical deficiency evidence.

canonical_inputs.limitation: Kennedy reviews B-vitamin roles in neurochemical synthesis; this does not establish dietary PLP provision or an intake-to-dopamine response in humans.

inventory.title: Acetylcholine Synthesis Support
inventory.mission: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.

canonical_inputs.role: Direct substrate combined with acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase to form acetylcholine
canonical_inputs.limitation: Choline is required and diet supplies it, but additional intake has not been shown here to raise acetylcholine synthesis in the human brain or improve attention.

canonical_inputs.role: Dietary choline-containing phospholipid that is digested and remodelled, producing circulating choline as one route to the direct choline substrate
canonical_inputs.limitation: Human tracer evidence establishes phosphatidylcholine as a choline-provision route; it does not show delivery to cholinergic terminals or increased brain acetylcholine synthesis.

canonical_inputs.role: Acetyl-group donor combined with choline by choline acetyltransferase to form acetylcholine
canonical_inputs.limitation: Acetyl-CoA is a cellular reaction substrate, not a dietary acetyl-CoA recommendation; ordinary dietary control of its availability in human cholinergic neurons is not established.

canonical_inputs.role: Nutritional precursor of coenzyme A, from which cells form the acetyl-CoA required for acetylcholine synthesis
canonical_inputs.limitation: Chronic ethanol-associated pantothenate depletion and rescue affected acetylcholine synthesis in rats; this does not establish that extra B5 raises brain acetylcholine in adequately nourished humans.

canonical_inputs.role: Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the brain choline resource available for acetylcholine formation; folate deprivation lowered choline and acetylcholine in studied mouse models, with SAM rescue supporting this upstream resource relationship.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Animal evidence is conditional on age, brain region and experimental context. Choline and acetylcholine concentrations were measured; methyl-dependent choline retention and the consequence for synthesis capacity are mechanistic inferences, not measured human synthesis flux. Folate is not a ChAT cofactor; extra folate above adequacy and cognitive benefit are not established.

canonical_inputs.role: Sodium supports the electrochemical coupling required for high-affinity CHT1 choline uptake, sustaining substrate-entry capacity for acetylcholine synthesis.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Transport-ion capacity does not establish that added dietary salt increases brain choline uptake or acetylcholine output. CNS homeostasis and membrane gradients intervene. Chloride is not assumed to have identical transport stoichiometry and is not independently admitted here.

upstream_dependencies.limitation: Human tracer evidence establishes phosphatidylcholine as a choline-provision route; it does not show delivery to cholinergic terminals or increased brain acetylcholine synthesis.

inventory.title: Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation

canonical_inputs.role: Long-chain omega-3 fatty acid incorporated into neuronal-membrane phospholipids
canonical_inputs.limitation: Diet can provide DHA for membrane incorporation. That does not establish an ADHD treatment effect or a human dosing rule from the porcine phospholipid comparison.

canonical_inputs.role: Choline can contribute methyl groups through the upstream methionine/SAM route to [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation). Methyl-derived LPC-DHA is a carrier used by MFSD2A for brain DHA delivery.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Human plasma isotopic enrichment is not absolute hepatic flux, net carrier supply or adult neuronal DHA incorporation. inventory.title: Glutamate Clearance & Recycling
inventory.mission: Clear and recycle glutamate efficiently so excitatory load does not overwhelm neural circuits.

canonical_inputs.role: Sodium supports the inward ion gradient coupled to EAAT-mediated glutamate uptake.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Established transport-ion capacity does not show that increasing dietary sodium increases brain clearance. CNS ion regulation and Na/K-pump energy supply intervene; transporter gradients are not inferred from a food quantity. No added-salt recommendation or clinical benefit.

canonical_inputs.role: Potassium supports EAAT countertransport and carrier cycling during glutamate clearance.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Established transport-ion capacity does not show that increasing dietary potassium increases brain clearance. CNS ion regulation and Na/K-pump energy supply intervene; transporter gradients are not inferred from a food quantity. No added-salt recommendation or clinical benefit.

inventory.title: Excitotoxicity Modulation
inventory.mission: Limit excitotoxic pressure when glutamatergic drive is excessive so neural stability is protected over time.

canonical_inputs.role: Dietary magnesium sustains the physiological ion pool required for voltage-dependent NMDA-channel block, a component of excitatory restraint.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Neuronal ion-manipulation experiments establish physiological capacity, not oral magnesium delivery at a pharmacological concentration, treatment of excitotoxic injury or benefit above adequacy. Brain homeostasis and membrane voltage remain determinants; more NMDA inhibition is not automatically beneficial.

inventory.title: GABA Synthesis Capacity
inventory.mission: Maintain sufficient glutamate decarboxylase capacity, and sufficient PLP cofactor to support it, so GABA can be synthesised from glutamate.

canonical_inputs.role: Substrate for GAD-dependent GABA synthesis
canonical_inputs.limitation: The evidence establishes glutamate as the GAD substrate, not that dietary glutamate or protein controls neuronal glutamate availability or human brain GABA synthesis.

canonical_inputs.role: Required cofactor for GAD-dependent conversion of glutamate to GABA
canonical_inputs.limitation: The evidence establishes PLP dependence of GAD, but not dietary PLP provision or an intake-to-synthesis response in humans.

canonical_inputs.role: Provides dietary B6 vitamers that pyridoxal kinase converts to PLP, the cofactor required for GAD-dependent GABA synthesis
canonical_inputs.limitation: Dietary B6 provision of PLP precursors is supported, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain GABA synthesis; PLP supports many enzymes and is not GABA-specific.

inventory.title: Synaptic Structural Plasticity
inventory.mission: Maintain and adapt physical connections between neurons through synapse formation, selective stabilisation, structural remodelling and elimination.

canonical_inputs.role: Choline supplies the phosphocholine headgroup used to build phosphatidylcholine, a membrane material supporting structural assembly.
canonical_inputs.limitation: This is membrane-precursor provision through the Kennedy route. Choline was not isolated in the gerbil spine experiment; no increased human synapse number or benefit from extra intake is established.

canonical_inputs.role: Uridine can supply CTP used in CDP-choline and phosphatidylcholine formation, contributing membrane precursors for structural assembly.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also contribute. UMP alone did not significantly increase gerbil spine density; that null structural result does not erase the precursor role. No ordinary-food dose or human structural benefit is established.

canonical_inputs.role: DHA supplementation increased hippocampal dendritic spine density in adult gerbils in the studied four-week exposure.
canonical_inputs.limitation: This is a preclinical structural state response, not proof of an indispensable intake or verified new synapse counts. It does not establish human synapse growth, ordinary-food equivalence or cognitive benefit. Developmental mouse marker and visual-response evidence is additional, context-specific support; marker abundance is not an ultrastructurally verified contact count.

inventory.title: Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation
inventory.mission: Recycle homocysteine to methionine through folate and B12 so methyl-donor supply and homocysteine control stay supported.

canonical_inputs.role: Methyl-group donor substrate for methionine synthase. The enzyme transfers that methyl group to homocysteine and releases tetrahydrofolate.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Necessity of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate does not show that raising its intake increases tissue methionine-synthase flux.

canonical_inputs.role: Dietary folate, including folic acid reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, is converted through the folate cycle to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor used by methionine synthase.
canonical_inputs.limitation: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker.

canonical_inputs.role: Cobalamin cofactor that carries the methyl group from 5-methyltetrahydrofolate to homocysteine during methionine synthase turnover.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Cofactor necessity does not show that extra vitamin B12 increases tissue methionine-synthase flux when stores are already adequate.

canonical_inputs.role: Dietary cobalamin is absorbed and processed intracellularly to the methylcobalamin cofactor used by methionine synthase.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Provision of vitamin B12 does not show that increasing intake raises tissue remethylation flux. Added vitamin B12 further lowered blood homocysteine beyond folic acid in pooled trials, which remains a circulating marker.

canonical_inputs.role: Sulfur-amino-acid substrate that methionine synthase remethylates to methionine.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Homocysteine is produced inside the methionine cycle. It is not a dietary requirement of this reaction, and methionine, the product, is not a dietary input for it.

canonical_inputs.role: Riboflavin supplies FMN and FAD used by methionine-synthase reductase to regenerate active B12-dependent methionine synthase.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Foundational human-enzyme cofactor provenance supports capacity; it is not a measurement of dietary riboflavin-induced remethylation flux, brain methylation or benefit above adequacy. FMN is also required; FAD is the endpoint of the displayed activation chain, not its sole functional cofactor.

canonical_inputs.role: FMN and FAD relay reducing equivalents in methionine-synthase reductase.
canonical_inputs.limitation: This is a biochemical cofactor target, not an independent oral FAD admission or food-content claim.

inventory.title: Betaine/BHMT Remethylation
inventory.mission: Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.

canonical_inputs.role: Methyl-donor substrate for BHMT remethylation of homocysteine to methionine
canonical_inputs.limitation: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

canonical_inputs.role: Dietary precursor that can be oxidised to betaine, the methyl-donor substrate for BHMT
canonical_inputs.limitation: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. canonical_inputs.role: Methyl-acceptor substrate that BHMT converts to methionine
canonical_inputs.limitation: Homocysteine is produced in the methionine cycle and is not a dietary input for this reaction.

canonical_inputs.limitation: Human purified-enzyme metal removal/reconstitution and ligand mutants establish zinc-dependent capacity. Dietary zinc supplies the same element, but no human extra-intake BHMT flux response, intake threshold or cognitive benefit is established.

upstream_dependencies.limitation: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux.

inventory.title: SAMe Synthesis

canonical_inputs.limitation: No ordinary-diet human dose-response demonstrating increased MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis was identified.

canonical_inputs.role: Direct adenine-nucleotide substrate for MAT-dependent SAMe formation
canonical_inputs.limitation: Diet does not supply ATP to MAT; no dietary ATP lever for SAMe synthesis is established.

canonical_inputs.role: Active-site metal ion coordinating ATP-derived phosphate groups during MAT catalysis
canonical_inputs.limitation: Human MAT structural and enzymological evidence establishes catalytic capacity. Ordinary food supply is distinct from measured MAT flux; no benefit from additional magnesium in replete people or universal methylation increase is asserted.

canonical_inputs.role: Choline can be oxidised to betaine, supplying methyl groups through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) for methionine regeneration upstream of PM3.

canonical_inputs.role: Choline can be oxidised to betaine, supplying methyl groups through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) for methionine regeneration within the integrated methionine cycle.

inventory.title: Glutathione Synthesis

Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.

canonical_inputs.limitation: In selenium-deficient adults, plasma glutathione peroxidase activity levelled off once intake reached about 35 micrograms a day. Intake above that plateau did not raise the enzyme further, and the study did not measure net oxidative pressure.

canonical_inputs.role: Catalytic metal in mitochondrial manganese superoxide dismutase
canonical_inputs.limitation: Human SOD2 requires manganese; dietary depletion experiments measured lower heart and kidney MnSOD activity in rats. canonical_inputs.role: These resistant starch forms provide substrates for specialist microbial degradation and cross-feeding; adding Ruminococcus bromii enhanced RS3 fermentation in one donor’s faecal community in vitro.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Cultures and one donor’s faecal rescue do not establish oral R. bromii efficacy, uniform human processing, equivalence to RS4 or clinical benefit.

canonical_inputs.role: Inulin supplies beta-(2,1)-linked fructan substrate to microbes with the corresponding utilisation machinery, supporting this glycan-processing capacity.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Utilisation genes, chain length, alternative substrates and resident organisms constrain the response. A supplied inulin substrate is not an indispensable intake, a guaranteed abundance shift, butyrate yield, mucus effect or clinical benefit.

inventory.title: SCFA Production & Signalling
inventory.mission: Maintain short-chain fatty acid production and signalling that supports gut barrier and brain communication.

canonical_inputs.role: Resistant starch reaching the colon supplies fermentable carbohydrate to microbial communities capable of its utilisation, supporting SCFA-production capacity.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Utilisation and product distribution depend on starch structure, processing, accessibility, primary degraders and cross-feeding partners. Evidence for one formulation does not establish an equivalent butyrate response from another preparation or whole food. No predictable yield, intake target or brain benefit is established.

canonical_inputs.role: The studied FOS/GOS mixture is a candidate microbial carbohydrate substrate; the corrected study does not sufficiently establish the existing PM-specific Capacity admission.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Requiring review: distinguish the studied mixture from individual FOS/GOS constituents, substrate utilisation from measured SCFA production, and SCFAs generally from butyrate. Ileal observations do not establish colonic absence; separate SCFA infusion and modelled estimates do not directly trace substrate conversion.

canonical_inputs.role: Fermentable polysaccharide supplying microbial SCFA production in human-microbiota culture experiments.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Pectin structure, purified preparation, donor community and enriched culture medium affect interpretation. Pascale is secondary synthesis; Bang is bounded primary culture evidence. Whole apples are not equivalent to the tested citrus preparation; no human brain or clinical benefit is established.

canonical_inputs.role: Acetate is a microbial fermentation product involved in metabolic or receptor-mediated signalling; this is product biology, not an oral requirement.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Endogenous microbial provision, absorption and compartmentation matter. Extra oral intake and benefit are not established by these studies.

canonical_inputs.role: Propionate is a microbial fermentation product involved in metabolic or receptor-mediated signalling; this is product biology, not an oral requirement.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Endogenous microbial provision, absorption and compartmentation matter. Extra oral intake and benefit are not established by these studies.

canonical_inputs.role: Butyrate is a microbial fermentation product involved in metabolic or receptor-mediated signalling; this is product biology, not an oral requirement.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Endogenous microbial provision, absorption and compartmentation matter. Extra oral intake and benefit are not established by these studies.

canonical_inputs.role: Inulin supplies fermentable carbohydrate for SCFA-producing microbial capacity; product distribution depends on community and culture or host conditions.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Culture conditions and community composition constrain production. Human inulin tracer estimates depend on assumed systemic availability; the human chicory-inulin trial did not significantly increase faecal butyrate. No fixed food yield, intake target or brain benefit is established.

traceability_gaps.limitation: Requiring review: distinguish the studied mixture from individual FOS/GOS constituents, substrate utilisation from measured SCFA production, and SCFAs generally from butyrate. Ileal observations do not establish colonic absence; separate SCFA infusion and modelled estimates do not directly trace substrate conversion.

inventory.title: Polyphenol Biotransformation & Mitochondrial-Relevant Metabolite Generation
inventory.mission: Enable microbial activation of dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites.

canonical_inputs.role: Immediate microbial substrate for the assessed urolithin-generation pathway.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Conversion depends on microbial community and may stop at intermediates. This does not imply universal conversion, increased mitochondrial function or benefit.

canonical_inputs.role: Hydrolysis releases ellagic acid upstream of microbial urolithin formation.
canonical_inputs.limitation: The human study tested a pomegranate-juice matrix rather than isolated equivalence of every ellagitannin; final metabolite generation varies.

canonical_inputs.role: Epicatechin supplies a defined microbial substrate for phenolic ring-fission and valerolactone-generation capacity.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Donor cultures do not establish a predictable whole-food conversion yield, mitochondrial effect or clinical benefit. Human apple-extract evidence involves mixed monomeric catechins, not isolated epicatechin efficacy. Do not generalise to EGCG or all procyanidins.

inventory.title: Vagal / ENS Signalling Modulation
inventory.mission: Maintain gut-to-brain nerve signalling through the vagus nerve and enteric nervous system.

canonical_inputs.role: This exact strain elicited vagus-dependent receptor-transcript and behavioural responses in mice.
canonical_inputs.limitation: The human placebo-controlled trial did not reproduce overall stress/cognitive benefit. No generic probiotic, fermented-food or nutritional-necessity claim.

canonical_inputs.role: Luminal glucose acted as a sensory stimulus in the tested mouse neuropod–vagal circuit.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Experimental neural response is not an optimal intake, an inadequacy threshold or benefit from more sugar.

canonical_inputs.role: Endogenous transmitter used by neuropod cells for rapid synaptic communication with vagal neurons.
canonical_inputs.limitation: This intracellular signalling role does not establish a requirement to eat glutamate or a human health benefit.

canonical_inputs.role: Linoleic acid engages intestinal fatty-acid sensing and vagal/brainstem nutrient signalling in the tested mouse circuits.
canonical_inputs.limitation: This is physiological nutrient sensing, not a beneficial direction or a need to increase linoleic acid. Human food-level circuit responses, vagal tone, ADHD and clinical benefits were not established. Foods generally supply esterified fatty acids released during digestion; the experimental free-fatty-acid stimulus is not a demonstrated food effect. More signalling is not automatically better.

traceability_gaps.limitation: The human placebo-controlled trial did not reproduce overall stress/cognitive benefit. No generic probiotic, fermented-food or nutritional-necessity claim.

inventory.title: Neurotransmitter Precursor Biotransformation & Availability
inventory.mission: Maintain gut-side processing that shapes neurotransmitter precursor availability.

canonical_inputs.role: Immediate substrate used by the microbial tryptophan-processing routes assessed here.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Substrate participation is not benefit from increased intake; host absorption, endogenous competition and microbial compartmentation differ from brain precursor delivery.

canonical_inputs.role: The tested pectin supplies cross-fed carbohydrate that redirects microbial tryptophan processing.
canonical_inputs.limitation: The experiment does not establish equivalence to all fibre or pectin foods, a human intake recommendation or brain neurotransmitter benefit.

canonical_inputs.role: Intracellular catalytic cofactor of the assessed E. coli tryptophanase enzyme.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Microbes can synthesise cofactors; this does not establish a host dietary vitamin B6 requirement or a beneficial direction of tryptophanase activity.

traceability_gaps.limitation: The experiment does not establish equivalence to all fibre or pectin foods, a human intake recommendation or brain neurotransmitter benefit.

inventory.title: Glucose Appearance Kinetics
inventory.mission: Shape the rate of post-meal glucose appearance so metabolic and neuroendocrine systems face manageable, predictable load.

inventory.title: Glycaemic Variability Regulation
inventory.mission: Limit glycaemic volatility so post-prandial glucose swings do not create unnecessary metabolic and neuroendocrine stress.

inventory.title: Insulin Sensitivity & Glucose Disposal
inventory.mission: Sustain insulin-sensitive glucose disposal so post-meal glucose clears efficiently without prolonged metabolic strain.

canonical_inputs.role: Magnesium availability supports insulin-receptor kinase signalling and insulin-responsive uptake.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Dietary-depletion evidence is preclinical; extra intake in magnesium-replete humans is not shown here.

canonical_inputs.role: Defined oral resistant-starch supplementation modulated clamp-measured insulin sensitivity and post-meal forearm glucose clearance in a small human study.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Preparation-, dose- and population-specific. The positive study used 30 g/day for four weeks in ten healthy participants; this is not an effective whole-food dose. Preserve the later 40 g/day type-2-diabetes null. SCFA mediation and universal benefit are unestablished; no brain or ADHD inference.

inventory.title: Cortisol Rhythm Regulation
inventory.mission: Maintain diurnal cortisol amplitude and phase so morning activation and evening downshift stay well timed.

inventory.title: Sympathetic Activation & Parasympathetic Recovery
inventory.mission: Maintain autonomic flexibility by shifting cleanly from sympathetic activation back into parasympathetic recovery.

inventory.title: Vagal Tone / HRV Regulation
inventory.mission: Sustain vagal tone so heart-rate-variability-linked recovery signalling remains robust under repeated stress exposure.

inventory.title: Adipose Endocrine Regulation
inventory.mission: Regulate adipose-derived endocrine signalling and local glucocorticoid responsiveness to communicate metabolic state and coordinate hormonal adaptation.

canonical_inputs.role: Defined oral DHA exposures can modulate circulating adiponectin, an adipose-derived endocrine signal.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Admission concerns a circulating hormone response in studied supplement/enriched-oil contexts. It does not establish adipose secretion, receptor sensitivity, universal benefit, ordinary-food efficacy or a food-effective dose. Mixture and carrier effects are not attributed to DHA alone; DHA-specific attribution uses the separate DHA-versus-EPA trial.

canonical_inputs.role: Microbial metabolite of dietary ellagitannins that raised circulating adiponectin and local adipose thyroid-hormone activation in rodent obesity models.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Endocrine engagement is demonstrated in animal studies only, using administered urolithin A. In humans, a rise in urinary urolithin A tracked visceral-fat loss but was not randomised, and four-month supplementation did not change fat mass. Production depends on gut microbiota and varies between people; no food-effective dose or human adipokine effect is established.

canonical_inputs.role: Dietary polyphenols hydrolysed to ellagic acid, which producer gut microbiota convert to urolithin A.
canonical_inputs.limitation: Food ellagitannin content is not a urolithin A amount. Conversion depends on hydrolysis and producer microbiota; some people produce little or none. Walnuts were the studied DIRECT-PLUS food; pomegranate is included from the ellagitannin ontology, not from an adipose endocrine trial.

traceability_gaps.limitation: Endocrine engagement is demonstrated in animal studies only, using administered urolithin A. In humans, a rise in urinary urolithin A tracked visceral-fat loss but was not randomised, and four-month supplementation did not change fat mass. Production depends on gut microbiota and varies between people; no food-effective dose or human adipokine effect is established.

inventory.title: Stress-Modulated Appetite & Reward Regulation
inventory.mission: Coordinate stress-responsive hypothalamic and reward signalling to regulate appetite and food-seeking motivation as physiological demands change.
